description: The data half of the logkit logging standard: everything an implementation must agree on that the record schema cannot express. Declares the canonical serialization (so three languages produce the same bytes), the timestamp derivation, the inbound level-alias map (so a native record maps to a canonical level deterministically or fails by name), the per-writer key configuration and the documented non-equivalences that make each native library's own output NOT a logkit record, the reserved `fields` keys, the human rendering's tokens, and the stream defaults. Record shape lives in log-record.schema.json; the normative prose standard is logkit-logging.spec.md. INVARIANTS: every `level_normalization.map` target is a member of the schema's level enum; `reserved_field_keys` is the complete set of `fields` keys with a meaning fixed by this contract; iteration order is declared array order everywhere, so identical input yields identical bytes.
inbound_key_map_notation: Each `native_writers[].inbound_key_map` entry reads source-path -> destination-path, both dotted from the root of their own object. A destination outside the record's root field set (`fields.target`) names the nested destination exactly; a source key absent from the map has no canonical home and is carried verbatim into `fields`.
native_writers_note: Each entry describes that library's own default JSON output, which is a property of the library version in use, not of this contract. An implementation pins the exact version it was written against and the conformance suite re-checks these key maps against it; a map that no longer matches the pinned version is a defect to fix here, not to work around in the implementation.

canonical_json.why: A published canonicalization is the only way three independent emitters produce identical bytes; the alternative is three hand-rolled serializers that agree until the first float or non-ASCII string. Each implementation uses an established JCS library for its language where one clears the dependency policy.
canonical_json.scope: `key_order`, `numbers`, `strings`, `encoding` and `whitespace` are RFC 8785 itself. `duplicate_keys`, `empty_containers`, `line_framing` and `write_atomicity` are logkit rules layered on top: JCS canonicalizes one JSON value and says nothing about how records are framed into a stream.
canonical_json.key_order: Lexicographic by UTF-16 code unit, at every object depth. Array element order is data and is preserved.
canonical_json.numbers: ECMA-262 shortest round-trip form, no exponent for magnitudes JCS renders without one; an integral float serializes as an integer (1.0 -> 1). NaN and the infinities are not JSON and are rejected at the API boundary, never coerced.
canonical_json.strings: Minimal JSON escaping: only the control characters, quotation mark and reverse solidus are escaped; every other character is emitted literally as UTF-8.
canonical_json.whitespace: None. No space after a colon or comma, no indentation, no trailing newline inside the record.
canonical_json.duplicate_keys: Impossible in the output: a key written twice on one record resolves last-write-wins before serialization, so the record carries one entry per key.
canonical_json.empty_containers: Omitted, not emitted. An absent optional field is absent - never {}, never [], never null.
canonical_json.line_framing: Exactly one record per line, terminated by a single LF (U+000A). The record contains no unescaped control character, so a line break can only be a record boundary.
canonical_json.write_atomicity: Each rendered line is handed to the sink in one write, so concurrent emitters never interleave partial lines.

timestamp.source: The emitter's wall clock at the moment the event is recorded, not at the moment it is written.
timestamp.timezone: UTC. A local-time or offset-bearing reading is converted; a reading with no timezone is rejected, never assumed to be local or UTC.
timestamp.note: Fixed width and zero-padded, so lexicographic order equals chronological order. Language runtimes that carry a monotonic reading alongside the wall clock (Go) format the wall clock.

procedure: Trim leading and trailing whitespace from the source token.
ASCII-lowercase it (only A-Z; never a locale-sensitive lowercase, which under a Turkish locale maps I to the dotless i and leaves INFO unequal to info).
A token absent from `map` is a normalization failure naming the token and the source - never a default, never `info`.

map.note: logkit has no trace level; the source token is preserved in fields.native_level.
Python's standard library defines FATAL as an alias of CRITICAL, both ordinal 50; a rename, not a demotion.
Ranks above fatal in zerolog and carries a distinct side effect; the source token is preserved in fields.native_level.

not_levels: A numeric level from a foreign scale is mapped by severity ordinal (see the schema's $defs/severity), and a value between two ordinals is a failure, not a rounding.
`off`, `disabled`, `notset` and `none` are writer configuration, not levels; a record carrying one fails normalization.

native_writers.role: byte writer only - logkit owns the record, the level set, the timestamp and the field names

writer_configuration.note: logkit SETS these names on the writer rather than relying on the library's defaults, so a default change upstream cannot drift the wire format.

non_equivalences: Nine `zerolog.Level` constants - trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic, no-level and disabled - against logkit's five; trace, panic, no-level and disabled have no logkit counterpart.
Fatal terminates the process and Panic panics; logkit's fatal has no side effect - it writes, flushes and returns, and the caller exits through the clikit taxonomy so exit codes stay in one place.
Fields are appended without de-duplication, so a key written twice appears twice in the output.
Insertion order, not sorted key order.
The default timestamp key is `time`, not `timestamp` (the default level and message keys already match the canonical ones, which is why this map renames only `time`).
`TimeFieldFormat` is a package-level global, so any dependency can change every logger's timestamp layout in-process; its default is second precision carrying the host's offset, not UTC milliseconds.

native_writers.role: byte writer only - logkit owns the record, the level set, the timestamp and the field names

writer_configuration.note: The JSON subscriber is configured to emit the canonical keys at the record root; event fields are not left nested under the subscriber's own `fields` envelope.

non_equivalences: Five levels, but TRACE..ERROR - there is no fatal, so logkit's fatal has no native counterpart and is carried as the record's own level.
The event message arrives as a field named `message` nested under `fields`, not as a root key.
Span context (`span`, `spans`) and `target` have no canonical home; they are carried verbatim into logkit's `fields`.
It is a tracing facade, not a logger: with no subscriber installed the same call emits nothing at all.

native_writers.role: byte writer only - logkit owns the record, the level set, the timestamp and the field names

writer_configuration.note: The processor chain is pinned by logkit: canonical renaming, UTC millisecond timestamping and canonical JSON serialization are logkit's processors, not the library's defaults.

non_equivalences: There is no timestamp at all unless a `TimeStamper` processor is in the chain; its default output is a Unix epoch float, and its ISO form carries microseconds, not the canonical three digits.
There is no level key at all unless an `add_log_level` processor is in the chain.
The standard-library level set it bridges is DEBUG..CRITICAL with no distinct fatal and with `warning` spelled in full.
Rendering is a processor chain, so two applications of the same library agree on nothing that the chain does not pin.

reserved_field_keys.meaning: The source's own level token, kept when the mapping was not an equivalence.

human_rendering.purpose: A person reading a terminal. It is a rendering of the same record, never a second source of truth, and no consumer parses it.
human_rendering.attribute_order: The record's own canonical key order for every key not in the header, with `fields` expanded in place and `schema_version` omitted.

value_quoting.otherwise: JSON string form, with JCS escaping
value_quoting.non_scalar: The value's canonical JSON form, verbatim

error.stack_position: one frame per line, after the record's own line

color.enabled_when: the sink is a TTY, the NO_COLOR environment variable is unset, and the configuration has not disabled it
color.invariant: Color adds SGR sequences and changes no other character, so the colorless rendering is recovered by stripping them.

streams.why: stdout carries the CLI's structured result under the clikit contract; a log line on stdout corrupts a caller parsing that result.
streams.concurrent_renderings: Both renderings may be enabled at once, each to its own sink - never two renderings interleaved on one stream. They are produced from a single record, so their field values are identical by construction.
